proof_summary: Any admissible \(m<2^{2^{33}+1}\) must satisfy \(\varphi(m)=2^{2^{33}}\); the bound \(2\varphi(m)\le m\) for even \(m\) makes \(m\) odd, and totient factorization then makes it a squarefree product of distinct Fermat primes \(F_i\), with \(\sum 2^i=2^{33}\) forcing the sole index \(i=33\). Thus every candidate below the fallback bound is \(F_{33}\) and forces its primality; when prime it is minimal, while otherwise no smaller candidate exists and the bounding power of two itself has the required totient divisibility.
